description.summary: GEM scroll bars drawn by the compositor

protocol.description:
On the Atari ST, GEM drew a window's scroll bars and the application told it where the sliders were. This protocol does the same on Wayland: a client reports how its window's content is scrolled, GemWM draws GEM scroll bars in the window frame, and asks the client to scroll when the user works them. Windows that don't use it get frames without scroll bars and draw their own.
Units are the client's own (a browser uses CSS pixels): only the ratios between position, visible and total matter to the compositor.

request.name: get_scroll
request.description: Create a scroll object for a toplevel's surface. The frame shows no scroll bars until the client reports an axis.

description.summary: stop drawing scroll bars for the window

request.name: set_axis

description.summary: report how an axis is scrolled

request.description: The visible part starts at position and is visible units long, out of total. A total of 0 removes that axis's scroll bar. Takes effect at once.

event.name: scroll_to

description.summary: the user moved a scroll bar

event.description: Scroll the axis so the visible part starts at position. The client reports the result with set_axis as usual.
